mcq.question: Why are the aquarium's getters declared `const`?

options.A: So that they return constant values only
options.C: To stop subclasses from overriding them
options.D: So they can be called on const controllers and promise not to modify the object

mcq.explanation: A const member function receives a pointer-to-const `this`. It can be called on const objects and the compiler rejects any attempt to change a member inside it.

mcq.question: `set_temperature_f` converts to Celsius and calls `set_temperature_c`. What is the main benefit?

options.A: Fahrenheit values are stored more precisely
options.D: The safety limits and logging live in one function, so the two setters can never disagree

mcq.explanation: Duplicated validation drifts apart over time. Delegating to one authoritative setter keeps a single source of truth for the rules.
